topics.name: Kinds of nouns, plurals and countable/uncountable

questions.rule: Simple present with she: verb + -s: practises.

options: Kolkata and Mumbai are big cities.
Kolkata and Mumbai are big citys.
Kolkata and Mumbai is big cities.
questions.rule: Two proper nouns joined by and take are; city ends in consonant + y, so plural cities.
To tell how she answered, use an adverb: calmly.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Riya is one person, so the present continuous is is + verb-ing: is talking.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: child has an irregular plural: children.
An adverb tells how you breathe: gently.
Yoga is singular, so the present verb takes -s: helps.
Subject + verb (keeps) + object + describing word.

chat: Do you do yoga every day?
options: Yes, I do yoga every morning.
Yes, I does yoga every morning.
Yes, I doing yoga every morning.
questions.rule: With I, the simple present has no -s: I do.

chat: How did the team play today?
questions.rule: good is an adjective; the adverb is well: played well.

options: The childrens' yoga mats are blue.
The childs' yoga mats are blue.
The children's yoga mats are blue.
questions.rule: children is already plural without -s, so add 's: children's.
After showed great we need a noun. The abstract noun of brave is bravery.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two days ago is in the past, so use the simple past: practised.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To tell how you bring it back, use the adverb gently.
Many needs a plural noun. The plural of woman is women.
Look! shows it is happening now: present continuous are doing.
An adverb of manner usually comes after the object: eats her lunch slowly.
Does + subject + base verb (no -s): Does your sister practise?

chat: What did you buy at the market?
options: I bought two loaves of bread.
I bought two loafs of bread.
I bought two loaves of breads.
questions.rule: loaf becomes loaves; bread is uncountable, so it has no plural -s.

options: He is reading in the library.
He is read in the library.
questions.rule: Present continuous: is + verb-ing: is reading.
its (no apostrophe) shows possession. it's means it is.

options: Arjun waited patient for his turn.
Arjun waited patiently for his turn.
Arjun waited patience for his turn.
questions.rule: To tell how he waited, use the adverb patiently.

options: Mindfulness reduce stress and helps us sleep better.
Mindfulness reduces stress and help us sleep better.
Mindfulness reduces stress and helps us sleep better.
questions.rule: Mindfulness is singular, so both verbs take -s: reduces and helps.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: brings calm and ___ needs a noun. The abstract noun of happy is happiness.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both my parents is plural, so the present continuous uses are: are reducing.
To tell how he walked, use the adverb carefully.
water is uncountable, so use a little. (a few/many go with countable nouns.)
Exclamation: What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb, ending with !

chat: How did you do in the yoga competition?
options: I did very good. I won second prize!
I did very well. I won second prize!
I did very well. I winned second prize!
questions.rule: Use the adverb well after did; the past of win is won.

chat: How many players are there in a cricket team?
options: There is eleven players in a team.
There are eleven players in a team.
There are eleven player in a team.
questions.rule: eleven needs a plural noun (players) and There are.

options: A hour of yoga makes me feel fresh.
An hour of yoga make me feel fresh.
An hour of yoga makes me feel fresh.
questions.rule: an hour (silent h), and the subject an hour is singular: makes.

options: Gold and silver are precious metals.
Gold and silver is precious metals.
Gold and silver are a precious metals.
questions.rule: Two material nouns joined by and take are; plural metals takes no a/an.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To tell how the baby was sleeping, use the adverb peacefully.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a modal like should, use the base verb: practise.

questions.after: the dishes when the phone rang.
questions.rule: Longer action going on in the past: was washing (Dad = one person).

questions.after: mats left in the yoga room.
questions.rule: mats is countable and plural, so use a few.
Plural subject (grandparents) takes the base verb go in the simple present.
team is a collective noun for one group, so it takes has here.

chat: Did you watch the yoga talk online?
questions.rule: yesterday needs the simple past: watched.

chat: Can you read the poem aloud, Rahul?
options: Yes, ma'am. I can reads it clearly.
Yes, ma'am. I can read it clearly.
Yes, ma'am. I can read it clear.
questions.rule: can + base verb (read), and the adverb clearly tells how.

options: Practising yoga every day keeps my grandmother active.
Practising yoga every day keep my grandmother active.
Practise yoga every day keeps my grandmother active.
questions.rule: The subject Practising yoga is one activity (singular), so the verb is keeps.

options: My brothers friends are coming home today.
My brother's friends is coming home today.
My brother's friends are coming home today.
questions.rule: Possession needs an apostrophe: brother's; friends is plural, so are.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To tell how he speaks, use the adverb politely.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After improve our we need a noun. The noun form is immunity.

questions.after: the newspaper before he goes for a walk.
questions.rule: A daily habit with he takes the simple present + -s: reads.
respond is a verb, so describe it with an adverb: thoughtfully.
What does + subject + base verb (teach, no -s) ... ?
Meena's shows possession with an apostrophe + s.

chat: Do we need more rice and plates for the party?
options: Yes, we need a few more rice and a little more plates.
Yes, we need a little more rice and a few more plates.
Yes, we need a little more rice and a little more plates.
questions.rule: rice is uncountable: a little. plates are countable: a few.

chat: Is your sister enjoying her new yoga class?
options: Yes, she enjoys it a lot. She goes there every evening.
Yes, she enjoy it a lot. She goes there every evening.
Yes, she enjoys it a lot. She go there every evening.
questions.rule: With she, simple present verbs take -s: enjoys, goes.
